paper_metadata.title: Quantum 2-Player Games and Realizations with Circuits

summary: The paper proposes a continuous‑time quantum walk algorithm for evaluating 2‑player game trees mapped to AND‑OR trees with theoretical runtime t ∝ √N. The authors simulate and physically implement small instances (2‑ to 5‑input trees) using classical analog circuits (PCB with R=10 kΩ and C=100 nF), observing decision times around 6–10 ms that match theoretical evolution curves. No gate‑based quantum hardware or qubit circuits are used.

experiments.description: Quantum 2-player zero-sum game realized as a continuous-time quantum walk on AND-OR trees, with theoretical analysis, circuit-network simulation, and PCB experimental realization for 2-, 3-, 4-, and 5-input game trees.

algorithm.variant: continuous-time quantum walk on AND-OR trees / quantum game trees
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial wave packet placed on the left side of the bottom runway; initial voltage state on left runway nodes in circuit implementation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary inputs are encoded by connected/disconnected switches or tree-node connections; the game tree alternates OR and AND nodes, and the root output is determined by the sign of the probability/voltage difference between right and left runway regions.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Evaluate the minimax value of a 2-player zero-sum game tree by mapping it to an AND-OR tree and determining the root node output (Alice wins if root=1, Bob wins if root=0).
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Hamiltonian of the AND-OR tree / quantum walk system constructed from the tree and runway graph; circuit-network Hamiltonian obtained via similarity transform from Kirchhoff equations.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic AND-OR game trees of sizes 2, 3, 4, and 5 inputs, including OR, AND, and mixed-depth subtrees; evaluated for all distinct input patterns shown in figures.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No external dataset; inputs are manually configured via switches/relays on the circuit board or by setting the corresponding tree connections.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical curves, circuit simulations, and experiments are compared by measuring the output sign after a critical evolution time; each experimental point is averaged over 5 runs with error bars.

hardware.framework: LTspice for simulation; custom classical circuit board / PCB for experiment

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Circuit parameters chosen as R=10 kΩ and C=100 nF; initial voltages applied to left runway nodes; relays disconnect initial voltages to start evolution.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Output computed from voltage difference between rightmost nodes and non-rightmost nodes, V_out(t)=sum_right |V_i(t)|^2 - sum_nonright |V_i(t)|^2, or equivalently sign of P_out.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical AND-OR tree evaluation / game-tree evaluation
speedup_claims.conditions: for 2-player zero-sum games mapped to AND-OR trees; reported for 3-input subtree, 4-input subtree, and 5-input game tree; also stated for the general quantum AND-OR tree construction
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports this as a quantum-walk advantage and validates it on classical circuit networks; the implementation is not gate-based quantum hardware.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical balanced binary AND-OR tree evaluation
speedup_claims.conditions: balanced binary AND-OR tree with zero error, expected time
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a cited classical complexity result used for comparison, not newly benchmarked in the paper.

speedup_claims.conditions: output time versus input scale N for the 3-input subtree, 4-input subtree, and 5-input game tree; also summarized for the 4 different AND-OR tree structures
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the measured output time satisfies t ∝ sqrt(N); the exact proportionality constant is not given.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N^0.754) for balanced binary AND-OR tree evaluation; alpha-beta pruning mentioned as classical baseline in general

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; experiments only demonstrate trees with N ≤ 5 inputs.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Authors claim O(√N) quantum walk evaluation of AND‑OR trees compared with classical O(N^0.754) algorithms, but no gate‑based implementation or resource estimates (qubits, gates, error correction) are provided.
limiting_factors: Not a gate‑based quantum implementation; experiments are classical analog circuit simulations of a quantum walk.
No qubit counts, gate counts, or fault‑tolerant resource estimates.
Claimed speedup is only quadratic O(√N).

notes: This paper does not use gate-based quantum hardware; it realizes the quantum-walk game tree on classical circuit networks (PCB) and via circuit simulation. No qubit count is reported because the implementation is not a gate-based qubit circuit.
The reported 'depth' refers to tree depth / graph depth, not quantum circuit depth.
Paper repeatedly claims 'quantum speedup' with scaling t ~ √N for evaluating AND‑OR game trees.
However the experiments are classical circuit realizations of the quantum‑walk Hamiltonian and not quantum hardware demonstrations.
